items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Well, I played some gigs with Lucky Roberts, yeah.

ctx.x: know what I mean? You couldn't work all that -- it was too much work. How could I work two places? The union wouldn't allow it, and how could I possibly do it?

So Lucky Roberts, he called me up and asked me, could I play some dates with him. Well, I'd heard of him. Lucky played for strictly rich people. Well, I had played for rich people on Fifth Avenue, because nothing but rich people used to live there. I played for rich people. But he had rich people out in Westbury and around there, and around Southampton, where the rich people used to be living at one time. Not now, but then. Nothing but rich people -- the Goulds, the Vanderbilts, the Astors, the Rockefellers and…

Well, he asked me, did I have any open dates? I told him I'd look and see. I was working at the time, but he said, I'd like to have you play with me, Scottie, let me know. So I went to my good old friend -- Cecil Smith wasn't playing then, he wasn't playing, he'd given it up. He was keeping a bar near the Amsterdam.
